lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: distinguishing similarity from congruence

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

items.prompt: Two triangles share two pairs of equal angles. Similar?

steps: The third angles must match too.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a parallel line

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-5, -5) about the origin with scale factor 2. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 15 becomes a side of length 60. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 1/4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 45; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 16

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 47° and ∠B = 50°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 47° and ∠E = 50°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
Yes, by SSS similarity.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a segment not through the centre, under a dilation with scale factor k …
choices: is mapped to a parallel segment k times as long
is mapped to a perpendicular segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment k² times as long
is mapped to a segment of the same length

items.prompt: Dilate the point (3, 9) about the origin with scale factor 5. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 18 becomes a side of length 90. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 72; the area is multiplied by 25
scale factor 1/5; the area is multiplied by 25
scale factor 5; the area is multiplied by 5
scale factor 5; the area is multiplied by 25

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 31° and ∠B = 30°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 31° and ∠E = 30°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that passes through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line through the origin with a different slope
is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a parallel line a fixed distance away

items.prompt: Dilate the point (6, 3) about the origin with scale factor 4. Give the image.
